finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl allows unauthenticated arbitrary file read. The attacker-supplied 'f' query parameter is joined onto /srv/files without containment checks, so '../' sequences escape the root.
finding.sink: files.go:13 os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)); contents written at files.go:18

trace.note: filepath.Join cleans '../' so f=../../../etc/passwd resolves outside /srv/files

finding.guards_checked: No '..' rejection, no Clean+prefix check, no filepath.Rel check, no os.Root/fs.FS containment, no authentication, no filename allowlist. Absolute paths are not an escape (Join concatenates under root).

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12 reads the 'f' query parameter unvalidated; files.go:13 passes filepath.Join(root, name) straight to os.ReadFile with no '..' rejection, Clean+prefix check, filepath.Rel check, or allowlist; files.go:32 registers /dl with no authentication middleware; files.go:18 writes the file bytes to the response. Joining does not prevent escape, since Join cleans '../' against root (e.g. f=../../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd).
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: /dl is routed unauthenticated at files.go:32, the attacker-controlled 'f' at files.go:12 flows unchecked into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, and the bytes are returned at files.go:18, so an anonymous client can read files outside /srv/files via '../' sequences.

finding.claim: No authentication or authorization on any route; server listens on all interfaces over plain HTTP, exposing /dl and /avatar to any network client.
finding.sink: Handlers download (files.go:11) and avatar (files.go:21) execute with no identity check

trace.note: /dl route registered with no auth wrapper
/avatar route registered with no auth wrapper
ListenAndServe(":8082", nil) binds all interfaces, no TLS

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware, no TLS, no bind-address restriction in this file. Deployment-level controls (proxy, firewall) are not visible in this directory.

verdict.guard_found: none. Routes are registered without middleware at files.go:32-33, and files.go:34 calls http.ListenAndServe(":8082", nil) with no TLS and no auth wrapper. The handlers at files.go:11-19 and files.go:21-29 perform no identity or authorization check before reading and returning files.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: /dl and /avatar are registered unauthenticated at files.go:32-33, and files.go:34 binds ":8082" over plain HTTP, so any anonymous network client can reach both handlers. Deployment-level controls such as a proxy or firewall are not visible in this directory, so the finding holds only if the service is reachable without them. The candidate also misses a more serious issue in the same file: download() at files.go:12-13 passes the unsanitized query parameter `f` to filepath.Join(root, name), which allows ../ path traversal out of /srv/files.
